fieldValues.title: Where an essay image comes from
fieldValues.decision_question: May an image paragraph show a remote image, or only a file stored in the repository?
fieldValues.context: The spec already stores binary files as SourceDocuments, attached to a record by an attaches SourceReference (I-101, I-102) and bounded by attachment_policy (I-107, I-111). srs-web has add_attachment and get_attachment_bytes. The core renderer today accepts http(s) image URLs in markdown. Precedent consulted: vignette a5fa4798 (attachments are not a place for big files); the sovereignty focus of the essay (vignette 19964824). Holon semanticops.com essay images, remedy fd1b4728.
fieldValues.friction: A remote image is not the writer's: it can disappear, change, or tell a third party who is reading.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Attached files only (recommended). For: the image travels with the essay, has a checksum and provenance, and works offline. Against: the writer must have the file.
B. Attached or remote URL. For: convenient for images already online. Against: link rot and reader tracking come back; two render paths to test.
C. Remote URL only. For: no storage. Against: the essay owns nothing.
fieldValues.key_requirements: The essay owns its images; one render path; readers are not tracked.
fieldValues.decision_statement: An image paragraph shows only an image file attached to the repository, never a remote URL.
fieldValues.rationale: Owning the file is the point of sovereignty, and one source means one path to build and test.
fieldValues.revisit_when: Writers routinely need images they cannot download or are not allowed to copy, such as licensed embeds.
